comments.author: @greatwhitenorthak1
comments.text: The title of this video is so inaccurate and perhaps only to entice those who know Alaska to wonder why this was titled this way. It's not impossible to live here as we are talking about a landscape that is 1/5 the size of the continental US States combined. Here in AK we have such a variety of landscapes, weather systems and certainly where snow is much varied and the light of the day depends what part of the Last Frontier you are talking about. Yes, living in remote locations around the state is very expensive but the vast majority of people who live here are connected by a road system and that is the lifeline that makes living here doable. I've been to all corners of this state to visit every metropolitan area, most villages and isolated settlements and homesteads. This state is a fantastic place to call home but it's not for everyone. I'm like many who came up here to try my hand and have called AK home for almost 40 years now. I have a cabin where there are beautiful mountain ranges, lakes, tundra and forests on all sides with so many places to hike and explore and NOT see a single human being. I live in the largest city where my main house is located and now as a snowbird I do spend the majority of the winters in the lower 48 and have a house down there. Why? Because I love to travel and explore the lower 48 as well as I also travel abroad regularly. But at the end of the day, its the remotes of this state, fewer fellow human beings I have to deal with, no ugly interstate highways and traffic congestions, and where one can live and not worry about whose land you are trespassing as a whole. You can camp just about anywhere including off the roadways where no one will bother you. People up here mind their own business but if you're one to come up here because you cannot get along with others, even AK is not for you. We still a reliant on others in times of need. I've seen those difficult folks and most either move back or they die in misery or even end up being kicked out or the law will take care of them. If I had lived over a 100 years ago, I would have no hesitation to live in the lower 48, but today its a madhouse with too many humans, urban growth and the vanishing wilderness were today, even visiting national parks is nothing but congestion and millions of bipeds and vehicles. OK, maybe I will say 'living in Alaska is impossible' to keep people from moving here and ruining this state as well (like whats happening in Hawaii today.) The 49th and 50th state are the only 2 states that I can say the whole state if beautiful as I've visited all 50 states since as a young man.
